argument_summary: The supportable position on the current admissible record is narrower than clean present-tense readiness: aggregate launch readiness is above threshold and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, but a named launch slice still has a material weakness and the draft runbook is not an approved mitigation. The packet should therefore be treated as a defense of certification only on a caveated basis, with the underwriting limitation explicitly disclosed and the monitoring/rollback concept described as draft mitigation rather than completed closure. That narrows the claim to one the record can support on a risk-weighted basis without overstating governance completion.
claims_about_business_cost: No admissible business-cost evidence is needed to resolve the audit issue. The practical governance cost of escalation can be reduced by accepting a narrowly framed caveated certification packet instead of forcing a binary choice between clean approval and full escalation.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not permit treating the draft runbook as full closure because it lacks the required owner and threshold, and the current record does not support a no-caveat certification. But the same policy framework does allow a certification position framed with a material caveat, because the unresolved weakness is identified, the disclosure obligation is clear, and public model-card and AI-risk guidance support documenting limitations and managing residual risk through monitoring during deployment. The audit concern is therefore best resolved by limiting the packet to caveated certification rather than treating it as an attempt to prove unconditional compliance already exists.
concessions: The current record does not support certification without material caveats.
The draft runbook is not an approved mitigation under the policy text because required governance fields remain TBD.
There is no admissible evidence in this record that the model-card language has already been finalized to disclose the underwriting limitation or that approved risk acceptance already exists.
Any packet language implying there are no known material limitations would be unsupported on this record.
